summary: Proof of Lemma 2.3, [p3-5] (and used in [p3-6]–[p3-8]): In a Boolean group, −x = x, so the translate is x + Ux, and the natural candidate for the intersection is ⋂_{x∈L} (x + Ux). But the text writes ⋂ₓ x + Ux, which parses as x + ⋂ₓ Ux (a single translate of the intersection), not as the intersection of the translates. The subsequent computation (x + U) ∩ (y + U) ⊆ (x + x + Ux) ∩ (y + y + Uy) req

Lemma 2.3, proof (Zorn's lemma application): The family 𝒫 is defined as a subset of τ, so its elements are open sets. Zorn's lemma requires the upper bound UI = ⋃_{α∈I} Uα to itself be an element of 𝒫, i.e., to be open. An arbitrary union of open sets is open in a topological space, so this particular union is in τ; moreover 0_G ∈ UI since all Uα contain 0_G, and the disjointness condition persist
